top_story: The reported U.S. bombing of a school in Minab on 30 September, which killed 120 children, has sharpened the sense that confrontation with Iran is no longer confined to military targets and is instead exacting mass civilian trauma likely to deepen public rage and harden retaliatory pressures. By 3 October, that wider climate of escalation was intersecting with security threats far from the battlefield, as two Iranian nationals appeared in a London court over an alleged bomb plot targeting Jews in northern England. The same day, UAE authorities said a flydubai co-pilot tried to seize lethal control of flight FZ1073 to Israel by attacking the captain with a crash axe, underscoring how ideological violence is reaching civilian transport corridors and diaspora communities. Taken together, the pattern points to a rapidly widening Iran-linked crisis in which civilian spaces—from schools to aircraft to communal life in Europe—are becoming the primary arena of risk.
